content:
nora: FYI we started getting 403s on SCIM user updates this morning after the infra RBAC cleanup. Example log entry from scim-worker:
```
PUT /scim/v2/Users/00u1... 403 - {error: decryption_failed}
cause: AccessDeniedException: arn:aws:sts::11111111:assumed-role/scim-service/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:11111111:key/abcd-efgh
```

diego: Confirmed. The role referenced in the error is the old scim-service role; our RBAC prune removed that role last night and a KMS rotation tightened key policy to only allow scim-service-v2.

hazel: Impact summary: ~64 failed provisioning ops across 18 orgs in the last hour. Failures are concentrated on users with extid tokens produced before the key rotation. Some errors are also InvalidCiphertextException due to mismatched encryption context keys.

nora: Immediate mitigation idea: short-term revert of the RBAC prune so the old role can decrypt. This is lower blast radius than changing key policy to open decrypt to more principals. Thoughts?

diego: Agreed. Revert RBAC prune for 30m window, run a small decrypt/rewrap job, then apply a migration to canonicalize contexts. We should also gate the revert with an approval from security.

securitybot: Policy audit: PR #732 removed inline policy kms-decrypt-scim from role scim-service on 2026-04-12T02:14Z. KMS key alias alias/redwood-scim was rotated at 2026-04-11T23:58Z.

hazel: Migration plan I propose: 1) Revert RBAC prune (hotfix) 2) Dry-run decrypt/rewrap job that attempts decrypt with legacy contexts ["extid-v1","extid-legacy","extid"] and logs which context succeeded 3) Re-encrypt with canonical context "extid" 4) Emit audit CSV with columns: org_id, user_okta_id, old_context, outcome 5) After 7 days of monitoring, remove old role and legacy contexts.

nora: Additions: must file privacy approval before mass decrypt (PII). Also add a metric scim.kms.decrypt.access_denied to alert on recurrence.

diego: I'll open the RBAC revert PR and add an expiration tag so the change auto-reverts in 24h unless manually extended. Hazel can you prepare the rewrap job and dry-run?

hazel: I'll build a MapReduce style job and a CLI flag --dry-run which only prints counts. Pseudo: 
```
for row in select users where needs_rewrap limit 5000:
  for ctx in ["extid-v1","extid-legacy","extid"]:
    try:
      plaintext = kms.decrypt(row.cipher, EncryptionContext={"extid":ctx})
      new_blob = kms.encrypt(plaintext, KeyId="alias/redwood-scim", EncryptionContext={"extid":"extid"})
      if not dry_run: update_user_extid(row.user_id, new_blob)
      emit_audit(row.user_id, row.org_id, ctx, "rewrap_ok")
      break
    except kms.AccessDeniedException:
      emit_audit(row.user_id, row.org_id, ctx, "access_denied")
    except kms.InvalidCiphertextException:
      continue
```

diego: Also add a retry queue for any users that still fail due to AccessDenied after revert window; we'll process after security approves permanent migration.

nora: I've filed COMP-803 for privacy signoff; include retention plan for the plain text only in memory and not persisted. Compliance will review within 2 hours.

securitybot: Incident INC-2026-521 created (severity: medium). Please post links to PRs and migration runbook here.

hazel: I'll include a per-org summary and a break-down of which encryption-context matched. Useful to know how many are legacy vs v1.

diego: Post-mortem action items: add KMS policy change checklist (verify role mappings first), include integration test that decrypts a test extid with both old/new contexts, and add alerting for KMS AccessDenied spikes after role changes.

nora: TL;DR: root cause = RBAC prune + KMS key policy rotation + historical context drift. Hotfix = temporary RBAC revert + rewrap migration. Medium-term = policy checklist, tests, and monitoring. I'll update INC-2026-521 with progress.

hazel: Running dry-run now, will post counts in 15m.
